Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS Posts Solid Growth in Quarterly Earnings Amid Robust Domestic Demand

Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS, a leading player in Turkey’s automotive sector, reported a steady rise in quarterly earnings on Thursday, buoyed by strong local demand and a resilient export performance. The company announced that net profit for the first quarter reached 2.1 billion lira, up 14% from the same period last year, while revenue climbed 18% to 36.4 billion lira.

The results were driven by increased sales of commercial vehicles and light trucks, which remain a cornerstone of the Turkish automotive market. Domestic sales volumes grew 9% year-on-year, supported by favorable financing conditions and ongoing urban infrastructure projects that have spurred demand for fleet vehicles. Export volumes also ticked higher, with key shipments to European markets remaining stable despite currency fluctuations.

“Our performance reflects the strength of our product lineup and our ability to adapt to evolving market needs,” said Ali Yılmaz, Chief Financial Officer of Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS, during a conference call with analysts. “Investments in advanced manufacturing and supply chain optimization have contributed to our efficiency and profitability.”

The Turkish automotive industry has experienced a recovery in recent quarters, following a period of volatility related to macroeconomic pressures and shifting consumer sentiment. According to the Turkish Automotive Manufacturers Association, total vehicle production rose 7% in the first quarter, with commercial vehicles accounting for a significant share of the increase.

Analysts at Yükseliş Securities noted that Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS’s focus on electrification and new model launches has positioned the company well for continued growth. “Their ability to maintain export volumes and capitalize on domestic demand is a positive sign in a competitive market,” said research director Meltem Kaya.

Looking ahead, Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS reaffirmed its full-year outlook, citing expectations for stable demand and ongoing efficiency gains. The company plans to continue investing in research and development, with an emphasis on hybrid and electric vehicle technologies. Shares of the company rose 2.3% in afternoon trading on the Borsa Istanbul.
